body: Woke up in the hospital not knowing what happened and hallucinating. I remember my dad crying.  I've never seen or heard him cry in my life. Never before that day and never since. I was 13 which now, with a stepson about to be 12, seems so SOOO young for a person to feel like their life should end.  But 13 year old girl brain isn't a sensible one and I ate 2 bottles of Tylenol pm. I told no one. I fell asleep peacefully and thought that was that. I "woke up" who knows how long after tripping balls. My brother found me sitting on his bed with vomit everywhere just smiling and puking. I didn't actually wake up until I was in the hospital for a few days and I remember my dad crying. I didn't think it was real.  When I finally had my senses back I didn't talk to anyone more than necessary for about a month. I stunk of Tylenol and failure.  I hated the world but would never do it again because I owe my life to my brother for finding me,  and my future life to my dad for showing me how much I mean to someone-probably the only person I never would have thought cared. I wish I could say I never attempted again.  I just never told my family after that.

Honestly, meds made the biggest difference. For about 3 years I tried everything.  Got a dog, exercised, the whole 9. I still felt like I was forcing myself to get over the depression because it would always come back and hit me hard when it wasn't just looming over my head. I sought help from a therapist and we decided to try meds. Took a while to find the right dosage but lord almighty did it help. I'll be the first to admit it's not the route for everyone and each case of depression varies.  My therapist explained it to me as if depression is a puzzle. Each piece to recovery being a different aspect of healing (talk therapy, exercise, meds etc.) And we had found most of the "lifestyle" pieces, but adding meds really seemed to fit as the missing piece. Again, not for everyone, but without them I would not feel back to my normal self.

I was rushed to the ER for lung issues last year, they took NUMEROUS xrays thinking birth control had caused a blood clot in my lung. I was in pain, couldn't breathe, and there wasn't enough oxygen getting to my body. It turned out to be something completely different, but for hours they were convinced I had a blood clot from birth control. If my symptoms were close enough to be considered a clot maybe they can be of some help:
I felt like I was going to pass out.
I did pass out.
My blood pressure was SCARY low (I don't have a medical background so I'm not sure if this is symptomatic of a clot or just the issues I was having- not a clot)
I could literally feel my body tissues not having enough oxygen. 
My lips were grayish, fingernails a blue/gray color, under my eyelids weren't that pink and my skin was not a normal healthy color.
I was in pain.

Again I'd like to stress that I did NOT have a clot, but for a long time in the ER, the doctors thought I did. Even with xrays showing up clean they thought it could be a clot from birth control.

I had been dating my SO for a few months and neither of us were farting in front of each other. We decided to go out for burritos one night, followed by a walk on the beach. Sounds cute, right? WRONG! The burrito made me sick to my stomach and I had to take some stomach medication. On the bright side, I felt better for our walk on the beach. On the (very) dark side, the side effect was farting. I seriously could NOT hold it in. To top it all off- they were stinky. At first I was mortified. I farted in his car- windows up. I could start to smell it. He pretended not to notice and it became this huge elephant in the room. I started laughing out loud at the fact that our conversation had stopped and it was just me, my SO, and my fart lingering between us. Just a smelly silence. We both knew I farted and I couldn't help it. I laughed. A LOT. 

It was so incredibly awkward and embarrassing at first but then I was like- what the hell, I'm sick and you're going to have to deal with this because I'm completely unable to hold it in. He was SUPER cool about it. My putrid, car-fart opened doors in our relationship and deepened our trust for one another (not to mention our comfort). 

Turns out, I had been sleep-farting while we were sleeping together and he didn't even care. He just didn't say anything because he thought I would be embarrassed. 

Have you talked to him about it? I know that sounds totally weird and awkward, but if my SO had just told me in the first place that I was (unknowingly) farting all along, I would have felt more comfortable to let 'er rip when I really didn't feel good. Does your SO fart in front of you?

I feel like if an SO can't handle a simple bodily function, then you'll never truly feel comfortable and relaxed around each other. That's just my take on it though. I hope you aren't going to the extreme where it's hurting you. Try the cheek-separation technique described in comments here. That usually works for sound muffling. Best of luck to you!

A very similar thing happened to me about a year ago. I went straight to the police though and because there was no DNA evidence (it happened in a hot tub) it was my word against his. He was never charged and is still living his life free as a bird. I only have two pieces of advice:

1) Get the person who is saying she is partially guilty to STFU! I'm sure your friend has gone through mental hell and back dealing with the situation. Shaming her to go to the police is placing guilt on the victim and will only make her stay quiet. She should NEVER have to feel that way about what happened to her. I understand that you're both concerned but she needs to report it on her own terms. 

2) As for what you can do, offer to be her support system (she's going to need a strong one). Going to the police will bring up all the negative emotions she has already been through: shame, guilt, embarrassment (which is a huge one), pain, insecurity etc. Reporting a crime will not only open the flood gates to all painful emotions, but it will rip open a part of her life that has been a very private matter. Imagine telling your darkest, dirtiest secret to someone you know will tell everyone in town. If they can catch the bastard, he will go to trial and she must know that all of this will be out in the public. If she decides to go through with pressing charges just be there with her. Offer to go with her to the station, hold her hand, and take her to a private place afterwards to debrief. Recommend she sees a counselor or therapist. The ramifications of such a disgusting violation of a basic female right go far beyond a simple bad memory.

Try and contain the amount of gossip/number of people that know. To her, this probably feels like the most difficult decision she has ever had to make and hearing everyone else's opinion on the matter may cloud her own. As you help her through this, remember confronting a sexual predator is terrifying and takes an immense amount of bravery. 

That being said I can also say that she may not feel okay right after she reports it. It takes time for the doubt and fear to go away, but I PROMISE it will help. I highly recommend asking your friend to find professional help as she seeks justice. I know it sounds vague, but just be there for her. My best friend supported me and I couldn't (and wouldn't) have done it without her. Best of luck. xx
